Re the traps: I read a good article the other day that I'll edit my comment to post in just a moment.

Edit: I'm paraphrasing 'What to Remember When Dealing with a Narcissist' from Down the Rabbit Hole.

Don’t believe the narcissist’s self-reports.

Narcissists will say anything they think makes them look good: most often lies or delusions.

Read between the lines.

Watch for weasel words and fuzzy logic. “I sold a book, and we bought a house.” You’re supposed to hear, “I sold a book, and we bought a house with the royalties.” The fact that the narcissist didn’t say that in the first place is telling. If she really did sell a book that brought in enough money to buy a house, she’d have told you how much she made or she’d go into detail about how rare it is for a book to earn that much and how special she is for writing it. If she says anything less–especially if she lets you infer the best part–it’s a red flag.

“Why wouldn’t she just lie about it?” you ask. Good question. Some narcissists will. Others are dimly aware that telling too many lies will get them caught and pilloried (again), so they stick to maximum deniability. (“I didn’t say we bought a house with the money from the book, I just said we bought a house after I sold the book. It’s not my fault you misheard me.”) And some of them like putting one over on you.

You’re not the first.

If the narcissist is past the age of six, they’ve hurt somebody else. And they probably hurt them in exactly the same way they’re hurting you. If needed, you might find their past contacts–friends, schoolmates, family members, students, co-workers. Narcissists are brilliant at isolating people who know too much, so look for hidden people: former friends who wandered away quietly, family members who aren’t estranged but just aren’t around much, people who worked for them for a while and then quit. And, perhaps, get in touch with those bitches who told such incredible lies about the narcissist and drummed the narcissist out of their circle because they were jealous of her/his talent. They likely know things you haven’t even started to dig up yet, and they might share once they know you’re not the narcissist’s sidekick.

“You’re not the first” applies online, too.

Look not only for people, but for sites: abortive early blogs, comments in other people’s blogs, forums and boards they abandoned, attempts at sockpuppeting. Even if a narcissist is new to the web, they almost certainly have a past that stretches beyond the moment they sashayed into your forum. Less web-savvy narcissists leave behind entire trails of attempts to establish themselves before they hit on a persona that works.

“That was long ago” doesn’t apply to narcissists.

Narcissists don’t improve. They may refine their techniques, they may become harder to catch, but they don’t become less malicious or toxic. Information about what a narcissist was like 10, 20, or 50 years ago is still relevant today.

Be doubly careful if the narcissist herself is the one trying to convince you that something is old news and doesn’t matter. Narcissists are prone to say that about things that happened ten minutes ago if it serves their purpose; it doesn’t have anything to do with the truth. In fact, it’s a red flag that you’re onto something.

Don’t give them money or personal information.

Regardless of how much (they say) they need it. A narcissist's lack of empathy will leave you high and dry when the narcissist benefits the most, which is usually when others are harmed the most.

Don’t underestimate them.

Narcissists have a single goal in life–their self-image. If they’re successful, they have networks of followers and dupes to give them money and aid in whatever they choose to do. If they’re unsuccessful, they are unencumbered by drains on their time and energy in the shape of friends, family, and work, and can spend 100% of their time and energy on getting revenge and digging up a fresh band of followers.

Don’t overestimate them.

Narcissists are often gullible, naive, and stunningly ignorant of anything outside their narrow circle of interests. (They’re often stunningly ignorant of things inside their circle of interests, since clearly they have already mastered the topic and don’t need to study more or keep up on new developments.) What looks like brilliant strategy is too often the result of being bugfuck crazy: They take chances because it doesn’t occur to them that they could lose, make huge demands because it doesn’t occur to them they they don’t have a right to ask for certain things, tell lies because it doesn’t occur to them that other people could see through them. Their “deep knowledge of human nature” is a set of formulas, and while it works painfully well most of the time, anything slightly off their charts will send them into a tailspin of projection. Remember that narcissists are formidable, but they’re not ninjas.

Their projections can be a powerful tool to use against them.

Get a narcissist frothing at the mouth, and she’ll let you in on a world of crazy regarding what she’s doing, why, when, how, and to whom. It’s better than getting a Batman villain to monologue.

This is a followup to my earlier post "Why can't I be a Dick?"

Arguments are usually classified by the types of techniques they use.

This is not the only way to classify arguments

They can also be classified according to social intent and other purposes

  • Social Status (beating the other person down with words) which often co-exists with other social purposes

  • Make the other person (rage) quit (trolling etc)

  • Discredit a person (in front of an audience)

  • Establish general credibility

  • Prove superior or inferior intellect or skill at argument

  • Prove or disprove a set of facts (as in a court of law)

  • To manipulate for an ulterior motive (Sales,Marketing, etc which is a special class of argument for social status)

  • Establish, Prove or disprove a hypothesis or theory (as in a science paper)

  • Establish the truth of something inside the context of a body of data

  • Establish the truth of something regardless of, or even despite other

  • Sport and entertainment.
  • As noted in The Dark Night (2008)

Alfred Pennyworth: Well, because he thought it was good sport. Because some men aren't looking for anything logical, like money. They can't be bought, bullied, reasoned, or negotiated with. Some men just want to watch the world burn.

  • Note that this is for personal reasons alone, and without regard or concern for the other person.

then we have

  • Establish the truth of something (without regard to status)

These categories overlap

  • For example, you can "Establish the Truth of Something" while at the same time discrediting a person, etc.

  • Arguing because of some element of social status does not immediately discredit the facts of the matter.

Importantly, you don't have to do it this way. Each one uses a variety of techniques for the purpose at hand.

Of course you can create your own categories, etc.

Thus, in some situations we have the context of "discrediting a person" because what they are saying is not in agreement "the rules of Science" or "Holy Scripture" (i.e. a particular "body of data") or "Everyone Knows". This can be according to a well known body of data, or some hidden standard.

"Hidden Standards" can act like a booby trap.

For example, in certain Islamic faiths, everything is the domain of God, and because of this anything that seeks to remove God from the world is an act of Satan. Thus democracy is an Act of Satan, and the USA is LITERALLY the great Satan because it is a democracy.

Their accepted "body of data" is the Koran, and this is the way these particular people interpret it.

Thus the important issue there is the social status of this particular body of information, Islam, etc.

The proper approach is to not invalidate Islam, since that is something Satan would do, but more likely a question like "Have men made mistakes in understanding the word of Allah?" Thus you avoid the booby trap.

Rules of logic are originally derived from a court of law.

Sometimes they are used in a way that makes for incomplete results when it comes to establishing an actual truth, because sometimes Social Status one way or another is more important actually establishing the truth, or the focus is on one theory only, etc.

Many arguments to establish "the actual truth of something" are actually arguments to establish social status instead ("See! I WAS right!")

This can have awful consequences when things go wrong. Mother Nature specializes in using "hard love"

In conclusion

Herding an argument in order to "establish the truth of something" is one way to eliminate general dickery. This takes more work, especially with people using hidden standards

This helps make Voat a better place, and builds a better community.

Paradoxically, you can achieve better social status by advancing an argument without needing to advance social status. Just focus on the basic facts and go from there
